headline: Socra provides a local voice layer for AI coding agents, enabling oral exams and interactive sessions
summary: The new tool allows developers to speak with their coding agents, using Piper TTS for agent speech and faster-whisper STT for user responses, enhancing understanding and debugging.
details: Socra is a new local voice layer designed for AI coding agents, initially developed to facilitate oral exams within an AI coding workflow. It aims to improve a developer's understanding by requiring them to verbally explain their project decisions.

The system uses Piper TTS for the agent's voice output and faster-whisper STT for transcribing the user's spoken answers. A minimal web page displays relevant context like code snippets or diagrams, with typing always available. It currently integrates with Claude Code and Pi, built on plain MCP tools.

Starting as a simple oral exam, Socra evolved into a multi-mode session, including a "mentor" mode. Key lessons learned involved managing conversational flow, such as speaking replies sentence-by-sentence to avoid perceived freezes during agent processing.

Technical refinements addressed issues like browser audio output going to sleep, which caused replies to start late. Language support was streamlined to focus on English first, with all language-dependent values centralized for easier future expansion to other languages like Spanish.

Voice selection was done through blind listening tests, prioritizing both quality and synthesis speed. Mode switching was also refined to ensure seamless handoffs between agent sessions, with logging added for better debugging.

For the mentor mode, Socra introduces a "scene" concept: a versioned JSON document that dictates visual elements (code lines, diagrams) and binds them to spoken steps. This approach ensures consistent visual state and precise error reporting for invalid scene definitions.
